The default color was chosen to compensate for the multiplier, and without it it doesn't look right at all. Even if that is changed to compensate, non-default color values will still appear way too opaque, in a way that the designers did not intend to.
If this PR is merged as is, what most users are going to experience is their collision shapes will be considerably harder to see through. It will severely impact visibility and be regarded as a regression of its own.

So I cannot in good conscience approve of this PR without having a proper system to convert existing scenes, such that the _final color_ is the same as before this PR. Not that I am sure on how to go about it.

> So I cannot in good conscience approve of this PR without having a proper system to convert existing scenes, such that the final color is the same as before this PR. Not that I am sure on how to go about it.

I thought adding initially a `debug_alpha` factor variable to `CollisionShape3D` and `Shape3D`, but it adds a whole new value in the inspector just to adjust the alpha of a color that already has an alpha. I think it's way overkill for the impact it really has (and people can always change the `debug_color` alpha themselves if it's too much.

I'll open some projects and take screenshots with the difference between my PR and 4.8.dev3 just to be sure that everything is still alright.

(oh, and yeah, it's possible to deactivate `debug_fill` if the collision shape view is not really needed.)

> > So I cannot in good conscience approve of this PR without having a proper system to convert existing scenes, such that the final color is the same as before this PR. Not that I am sure on how to go about it.
> 
> I thought adding initially a `debug_alpha` factor variable to `CollisionShape3D` and `Shape3D`, but it adds a whole new value in the inspector just to adjust the alpha of a color that already has an alpha. I think it's way overkill for the impact it really has (and people can always change the `debug_color` alpha themselves if it's too much.

But if it's _absolutely_ necessary, I can add the feature back. (but I still find the idea of having two ways to control alpha (`debug_color`'s alpha and `debug_alpha` as an alpha factor on top of it) is really overkill.)

@smix8 wrote [in the Godot Chat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/editor?msg=z7frzp3kxbaXwp8vo):
> My main concern with this is ..
>
> how many new complains will we get about changing the visuals for everyone compared to the few complains about it being hard to see :gdpray:
>
> like if I had a large project where I now needed to fix every single node's debug color manually again after this change I would start a riot.

I tend to say that every collision shape `debug_fill` shouldn't be necessarily on, but I understand that the default behavior and that people keep it that way because it's so faint as it currently renders.

We could maybe add a new project setting: `debug/shapes/collision/shape_color_3d_modulate` set to a default value of `Color(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0625)`?

At the cost of a single project setting, we could keep the editor behavior as is AND not add any new property to `CollisionShape3D` and `Shape3D`.

Debug shapes from child scenes show up more transparent than shapes in the current scene. Are those nested shapes still going to have some fixed additional transparency? Any thoughts on adding that as a setting as well?

> Debug shapes from child scenes show up more transparent than shapes in the current scene. Are those nested shapes still going to have some fixed additional transparency? Any thoughts on adding that as a setting as well?

I think it's outside of the scope of this PR. But I'll make sure that, by default, it doesn't change the current behavior.
